photo_derived_dimensions.gpio_mating_datum: Photo-registered underside -Y header, centre Y3.60; rows2.33/4.87 at2.54 pitch. HAT turns180degrees relative to Pi in the assembled photo; connector body height is unverified.

meta.board_drawing_coordinate_system: Origin at lower-left of 65 x 30.2 PCB outline; X right; Y up; Z=0 at PCB bottom. Joystick left, keys right, GPIO on underside near -Y.
accuracy_notes: Published board size, mounting hole pitch, mounting drill radius and active display area are the dimensioned constraints.

The 26.16 x 29.22 panel drawing is a related official Waveshare panel datasheet; a matching part number for the original HAT was not published. Panel stack dimensions and the shifted active area are conditional estimates.

The female header is surface mounted on the underside along -Y. Its 8.5 mm body height is an adjustable visual estimate, not a verified manufacturer dimension or an assertion about the assembled board spacing.
Button, joystick, FPC, via and passive placement and heights were estimated from product photos; these are visual CAD geometry, not a manufacturing drawing.

The underside schematic identifies three resistors, C1 and S8050 Q1. Their package dimensions are estimates and positions follow the registered official back photograph. R3 is marked102 and R2 is marked103.

Copper routes follow only visible photo contours, with6micrometre mask relief; the FPC copper crosshatch is visual reconstruction. The dark flex patch is not asserted to be an independently identified IC.

KEY1/KEY2/KEY3, primary back legends, Waveshare logo approximation and resistor codes have thin STEP-visible white ink geometry. Fine FPC manufacturing typography and minor artwork remain texture-only.

Visible PCB solder lands and the twelve flex fingers have a silver tin/nickel finish following the official photos; protected internal socket contacts and the amber flex copper/rings retain their gold/copper appearance.
meta.printed_legend_scale_status: Glyph runs normalized to photo-measured widths; main logo and registered mark have independent photo footprints. Primary legends retain STEP-visible glyph solids.
